jobs.title: Director, AI Solutions Strategy & Planning
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Instacart is building a new, distinctive pillar of the Instacart Platform — an emerging portfolio of AI-driven retailer solutions — and the go-to-market infrastructure to scale it is being built right now. The opportunity is real, but translating it into scalable commercialization frameworks, pricing strategies, and GTM plans requires specialized expertise and a dedicated strategy and planning leader. We're hiring a Director of AI Solutions Strategy & Planning to lead that work end-to-end. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise strategy and frontier AI, working cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Marketing, Legal, and Customer Success to shape how Instacart becomes the preferred technology partner for grocery retailers.

What You'll Cook Up In Your First Year

A comprehensive GTM strategy for Instacart's AI-driven solutions is defined and in motion — spanning consumer experiences, ecommerce analytics, and enhanced retailer workflows — with clear positioning, pricing frameworks, and retailer onboarding playbooks in place.
Cross-functional alignment across Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Legal is established, with governance forums running smoothly and transparent decision-making processes embedded across GTM and product teams.
Pilot programs and experimentation frameworks are launched and producing real impact — validating AI-powered products with real retailer feedback and iterating based on measurable performance metrics.
Sales teams are enabled and equipped with AI-specific strategies, enablement materials, and training programs that accelerate adoption and pipeline velocity.
Market intelligence and competitive analysis are regularly informing product and commercialization decisions, keeping Instacart's AI solutions competitive, scalable, and aligned with evolving retailer needs.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have Pantry Staples (Minimum Qualifications)

8+ years of experience in strategy, product commercialization, or GTM planning, with a proven track record of defining and executing strategies for emerging offerings and driving measurable market impact.
Experience developing GTM strategies for AI-powered products, retailer solutions, or enterprise technology platforms.
Deep understanding of AI technologies, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business value for diverse audiences.
Expertise in product positioning, pricing frameworks, and solution packaging.
Strong analytical capabilities, including experience with modeling, forecasting, and evaluating solution performance.
Exceptional cross-functional leadership skills with a track record of influencing stakeholders across Product, Sales, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for simplifying complex concepts and presenting to internal and external audiences.
Strong quantitative skills to help inform opportunity sizing, impact assessment, pricing strategy, and financial outlook in partnership with cross-functional peers.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and rapidly changing environments, with a focus on iterative learning and innovation.

Optional Garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

Familiarity with conversational AI, ecommerce analytics, or retail technology applications.
Advanced knowledge of AI product monetization models, including subscription, usage-based, and value-based models.
MBA or advanced degree in business, technology, or a related field.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here. Currently, we are only hiring in the following provinces: Ontario, Alberta, British Columbia, and Nova Scotia.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

SLSQ427R938

Do you want to help solve the world's toughest business problems with Data and AI? This is what we do every day at Databricks.

We are looking for an Enterprise Sales Director to lead our growing Public Sector business in Ottawa. Leading a team of Enterprise Named and Strategic Account Executives, you will be measured by achieving your team's overall quota and growing Databricks' consumption. This is a team of account executives that are passionate about building a data ecosystem, technically knowledgeable, and have a strong desire to drive value for our customers.

You will oversee the sales team, implementing sales plans, expanding existing business and delivering accurate sales forecasting and reporting.

This is a fantastic opportunity to build upon a highly successful team achieving significant year on year growth, in a fast growing business which is a hugely impactful part of the Canadian sales organization. We are looking for owners, who will go the extra mile and want to be the very best at what they do.

The Impact You Will Have

Lead a team of account executives, ensuring you coach them to develop the skills and behaviors they will need to succeed
Establish company territory plans, team structure, individual quotas and patches for your team, including investment capacity requirements
Report on revenue forecast and strategic GTM programs
Partner with cross-functional teams to manage a complete revenue and customer success process
Inspire a culture of teamwork, leading with value and achieving desired customers outcomes
Develop trust-based relationships with customers and partners to ensure long-term success
Encourage learning and ongoing understanding of technical product details and our future product roadmap
Establish a revenue growth and investment plan in the first 90 days
Deliver our strategic growth plans, in collaboration with the other function leaders across Canada, ensure forecast accuracy and a predictable, high-growth business

What We Look For

Experience as a high-growth enterprise software sales leader with experience leading sales teams serving Named and Strategic customers within the Data, AI, Cloud, or SaaS Sales Industry, specifically within the Public Sector space.
History of exceeding sales quotas in similar high-growth technology companies
Ability to engage with and hire sales talent in the market
Focus and emphasis on methodology-based sales coaching, MEDDPIC and a Challenger mentality
Experience of value-based sales with both the business and IT stakeholders including C suite
Experience in leadership roles focused on managing sales organisations to influence, develop, and achieve objectives within Data, AI, Cloud, or SaaS sales
Extended Executive relationship network with key customers.
Knowledge of the partner ecosystem to help grow Enterprise strategic territories
Success implementing strategies for consumption and commitment-based sales revenue models.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and Instagram.

jobs.title: Director of Customer Success
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview

Instacart's Enterprise Solutions team partners with Global grocery and retail chains to power their digital commerce through StorefrontPro, Enterprise API (Fulfillment and Ads), CarrotAds, and adjacent Enterprise Solutions products. We're seeking a Director, Customer Success to lead the Customer Success organization — accountable for post-live value realization across the enterprise software portfolio.

In this highly visible role, you will lead senior managers and Customer Success Managers who serve as the strategic advisor of Instacart to retailer executives. You'll own retailer value realization, measured through adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score coverage, at-risk portfolio management, CSAT, and QBR quality across the portfolio. You'll partner closely with Business Development, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness. You'll also partner with Enterprise Solutions Delivery, Technology leadership, and Product on portfolio strategy, retailer signal, and roadmap adoption.

This is a roll-up-your-sleeves leadership opportunity for someone who has personally led the transformation of CS from reactive enablement toward proactive business advisory, can hire and develop senior consultative talent, and thrives in a fast-paced, BD-led commercial environment with shared standards rather than rigid process. The role reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Solutions , and is remote across the United States and Canada with a preference for proximity to Toronto for key cross-functional collaboration.

About The Job

Lead the Customer Success organization for the Enterprise Solutions portfolio — owning value realization, outcomes end to end, and partner closely with BD, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness.Build and develop a senior consultative CS bench by hiring, sponsoring, and ramping Customer Success Managers who engage with retailer executives on ecommerce strategy, merchandising, and operations and who can credibly influence retailer P&L outcomes and roadmap adoption.
Manage senior managers leading segments, setting standards for what good looks like across the CSM’s — including QBR quality, growth planning, executive engagement, and renewal execution.
Operate in a BD-led commercial environment as a true commercial peer to BD — preserving BD's ownership of the primary commercial relationship while owning post-sale accountability and surfacing churn, expansion, and escalation signal early and clearly.
Partner with the Director of Enterprise Architecture & Engineering on shared-account coordination — ensuring the cross-org account team ( CS + Technical Account Managers (TAM’s) ) functions as one team to the retailer despite the functional ownership, with co-authored protocols and clean escalation paths.
Define and enforce the CSM/TAM boundary based on segmentation — CSM’s lead retailer-executive engagement, value realization, and growth planning, while TAM’s own technical delivery, configuration, and issue resolution, so that CSM capacity stays focused on strategic advisory, not technical execution.
Own the consultative transformation roadmap — talent strategy, comp structure, operating cadence, and tooling shifts required to evolve CS from a feature-enablement function into a strategic business advisory function.
Partner with the Director of Retailer Delivery on the implementation-to-success motion as a managed lifecycle (not a document handoff) — ensuring CS is engaged early, named handoff criteria are met, and accounts transition cleanly into early-lifecycle growth ownership.
Operationalize the retailer segmented model in CS — applying high-touch coverage and scaled/digital-first models, with clear exception protocols and capacity guardrails.
Build a structured retailer-signal feedback loop into Product — using CS engagements to surface durable patterns (not anecdotes), instrument adoption of roadmap items, and hold CS accountable for adoption outcomes.
Apply AI augmentation to scale CS coverage and quality without linear headcount growth — including health monitoring, account-prep automation, QBR/insight generation, and signal triage — partnering with the Technical org on tooling roadmap and adoption.
Represent the post-sale narrative for the portfolio to senior leadership — integrating retention, growth, churn risk, executive-account temperature, and pipeline outlook — and serve as the Director-level escalation point for retailer relationships when CSM-led engagement is insufficient.

About You

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years of enterprise customer success, account management, or post-sale leadership at a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.
Direct, accountable leadership of a customer success organization responsible for adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score, at-risk portfolio, CSAT, QBR quality and support BD with GRR, NRR, and expansion.
Track record of managing managers with demonstrated ability to set standards and develop senior leaders without micromanagement.
Ownership of a CS book of business or post-sale P&L of meaningful scale (e.g., $1000M+ ARR) with documented outcomes on Adoption, NRR, GRR, or expansion.
Proven success operating in a BD- or Sales-led commercial environment — clear instinct for where the CS lane begins and ends, comfort with shared standards rather than rigid RACI/process.
Demonstrated executive presence with enterprise customer counterparts (VP / SVP / C-level), including the ability to deliver hard news, navigate escalations, and rebuild trust after issues.
Experience designing and operating segmented CS coverage models (high-touch for strategic accounts, scaled/digital for the long tail), including capacity planning and exception handling.
Hands-on experience hiring senior CS talent — with a clear point of view on profile, comp, and ramp.
Strong background having operated in an end to end post sales service delivery ecosystem with strong CS interaction with Business Development/Sales, Delivery, Technical and Product teams. Preferred Qualifications
Experience transforming a CS function from reactive enablement into proactive business advisory, including the talent, comp, operating-model, and tooling changes required (not a renaming exercise).
Track record of building or scaling seasoned strategist roles inside a CS org — including hiring profile, ramp, comp design, and integration with the rest of the account team.
Experience operating with a separate technical TAM function on shared enterprise accounts — including co-authoring cross-org protocols and managing escalations across an org boundary.
Background applying AI to CS workflows — health monitoring, account preparation, QBR generation, signal triage — with measurable impact on coverage, throughput, or quality.
Familiarity with the BD/CS interface in commercially complex enterprise sales motions, including renewals, multi-product expansion, and shared-account operating norms.
Deep familiarity with enterprise retail, grocery, ecommerce platforms, retail media, or adjacent complex B2B domains — including how large retailers evaluate, adopt, and scale technology solutions.
Experience instrumenting retailer signal into structured product feedback (not anecdotal) and partnering with Product leaders on adoption accountability.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director, Administrative Services is responsible for providing strategic leadership, direction and expertise in support of the WCB's administrative services functions. This includes responsibility for the WCB's Corporate Records, Corporate Security and Facilities functions, and accountability for security of people and assets, information governance, and stewardship of corporate facilities.

Job Duties

Leads the Corporate Records, Corporate Security and Facilities functions, ensuring programs and services support organizational objectives and operational requirements.

Provides management, leadership, guidance, support and direction to staff in the functional areas.

This includes responsibility for hiring, conducting performance reviews, labour relations, performance development, coaching and deciding on disciplinary action up to and including dismissal where necessary.

Provides strategic advice and recommendations to executive leadership regarding records and information management, physical security, emergency preparedness and facilities management.

Participates in organizational emergency preparedness and emergency response activities, and ensures appropriate plans and resources are in place.

Leads the planning and management of departmental operating and capital budgets, and ensures effective oversight of financial, human, information and physical resources.

Establishes departmental priorities, objectives and performance measures, and monitors results to support continuous improvement and effective service delivery.

Directs long-term planning of corporate facilities, including facility development, infrastructure renewal and capital improvements.

Oversees corporate security programs and services to support the protection of employees, facilities and organizational assets.

Leads and supports the organization's records and information management program, and ensures compliance with legislative and organizational requirements.

Manages procurement, contracts and vendor relationships.

Builds and maintains effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Performs other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

University degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management or a related discipline

Minimum ten (10) years of progressive management experience in administrative services, or related fields

Knowledge of legislation, regulations, standards and best practices related to administrative services, including records and information management, security, facilities management, emergency preparedness and occupational health and safety

Experience developing strategic and operational plans, establishing priorities and aligning resources to achieve organizational objectives

Experience developing and managing operating and capital budgets, contracts, procurement activities, vendor relationships and major projects

Superior leadership, communication, negotiation and relationship management skills

Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills

Ability to influence, persuade and achieve consensus with diverse stakeholders

Ability to manage challenging and sometime confrontational situations with tact and diplomacy

Ability to manage highly confidential and sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment

Ability to organize and prioritize workload while managing multiple demands and competing priorities

Available to address facility and security related issues outside regular working hours, as required

Proficiency in the use of personal computers, Windows-based software, and other technology platforms relevant to the position

The ability to communicate proficiently in both official languages (English and French) is an asset but is not required

Additional Information

A satisfactory criminal record check and verification of education will be required for the successful candidate.

The WCB is committed to building a skilled, diverse workforce with equitable representation of Indigenous persons, visible minorities, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ persons and members of other equity-seeking groups. Applicants are encouraged to indicate in their covering letter or resumé if they are a member of these groups.

jobs.title: Director, Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations
jobs.description:
Director, Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations – Canada

Expleo Group Canada | Montreal, Quebec | Onsite

Build the business. Lead the team. Open new markets.

Expleo Group Canada is seeking an accomplished, commercially driven Director of Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations
to lead our Canadian aerospace operations and accelerate our expansion into professional engineering and technical services.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced engineering business development professional who combines the commercial instincts of a proven new-business hunter with the leadership capabilities of an effective operational manager.

We are seeking a player-coach - someone who can personally develop and close new business while leading a small team, strengthening customer relationships, elevating operational standards, and building a high-performance culture.

Our Canadian business has an established presence supporting aerospace production, assembly, manufacturing, and technical operations. Our next phase of growth is focused on expanding into higher-value engineering and professional technical services, including engineering staffing, specialized technical consulting, and project-based engineering solutions.

The successful candidate will bring established engineering or aerospace industry knowledge
, executive-level business presence, a strong understanding of engineering staffing and services, and a demonstrated history of opening new customer relationships.

This is not a position for someone who wants to manage an existing portfolio from behind a desk. We need a leader who can run the business while actively creating its next phase of growth.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering / Aerospace Business Development & Market Expansion (80% focus)

Lead executive-level customer discussions, strategic business reviews, commercial negotiations, and major account development initiatives.
Personally identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities with aerospace OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, and other aerospace and aviation organizations.
Leverage established industry relationships to gain access to engineering directors, program leaders, procurement executives, and senior decision-makers.
Develop new customer relationships through proactive prospecting, strategic networking, direct outreach, referrals, and in-person engagement.
Develop a qualified pipeline of new engineering business and consistently deliver measurable growth in revenue and profitability.
Build a sustainable market presence that positions Expleo as a credible engineering and technical services partner within the Canadian aerospace industry.

Canadian Operations & Business Leadership (20% focus)

Provide hands-on leadership for account team.
Lead, coach, and develop local account management teams, working with HR to establish clear expectations for performance, accountability, professionalism, and customer service.
Strengthen operational discipline, customer responsiveness, business communication, and leadership effectiveness across the Canadian organization.
Establish a consistent, professional, and commercially focused approach to customer meetings, business reviews, escalations, and operational reporting.
Oversee customer account performance, service delivery commitments, resource planning, and business profitability in partnership with delivery, recruiting, finance, and HR.
Build a collaborative, results-oriented culture that balances strong customer service with commercial growth and operational excellence.
Ensure effective coordination between local operations and Expleo's broader North American and global leadership teams.
Provide regular business performance updates and strategic recommendations to North American leadership.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in aerospace business development, engineering staffing, technical consulting, or engineering services, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
Proven success personally developing and closing new aerospace engineering staffing or professional technical services business.
Strong understanding of white-collar aerospace engineering disciplines, technical workforce requirements, and the commercial models used in engineering staffing and outsourced services.
Demonstrated experience leading a branch, regional operation, business unit, or commercial team with accountability for business growth and operational performance.
Established knowledge of the Canadian aerospace market, particularly the Quebec and Montreal aerospace ecosystem.
Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior engineering, operations, procurement, and executive stakeholders.
Proven ability to generate new opportunities independently rather than relying primarily on inbound requisitions or existing customer relationships.
Experience managing revenue targets, sales pipelines, commercial negotiations, account profitability, and business performance.
Strong leadership capabilities, including coaching, performance management, team development, and the ability to establish accountability.
Executive-level communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
Ability to balance strategic business development with hands-on operational leadership.
Professional fluency in French and English, both written and spoken, subject to the documented requirements of the position. French is essential for leading local operations and communicating with Quebec-based employees and customers. English is required for regular business discussions, commercial negotiations, and collaboration with customers and leadership outside Quebec, where these responsibilities cannot reasonably be reassigned.
Legally authorized to work in Canada without requiring employer immigration sponsorship.
Willing to work regularly on-site in the Montreal office and travel to customer locations as business needs require.
a multinational engineering, aerospace, or consulting organization.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Management, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

The Leader We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who brings both commercial credibility and operational leadership.
You have personally opened doors, developed relationships with engineering decision-makers, negotiated business, and delivered measurable sales results.
You are equally comfortable presenting to an aerospace executive, visiting a customer production facility, coaching an account manager, and addressing an operational performance issue.
You understand that leadership requires visibility, accountability, professionalism, and follow-through.
Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to build a business - not simply maintain one.

jobs.title: Director - Leadership Rotation Program
jobs.description:
Holman is a global automotive leader that serves both commercial and consumer clients The Holman Way by always doing the right thing for our people, our customers, and the community since 1924. The Holman story began nearly a century ago as a single Ford dealership in New Jersey. Today, Holman, headquartered in Mount Laurel, New Jersey, is one of the largest family-owned automotive service organizations in North America with more than 6,500 employees across North America, the UK, and Germany.

Holman delivers a unique range of automotive-centric services including industry-leading fleet management and leasing; vehicle fabrication and upfitting; component manufacturing and productivity solutions; powertrain distribution and logistics services; commercial and personal insurance and risk management; and retail automotive sales as one of the largest privately owned dealership groups in the United States. Guided by its deeply rooted core values and principles, Holman is continuously Driving What’s Right .

The Holman Leadership Rotation Program (HLRP) is a highly selective opportunity intended for leaders who have demonstrated the capability, aspiration, and potential to assume significantly broader leadership responsibility and who are committed to building leadership capability beyond their current expertise. Participants undertake rotational assignments aligned to Holman's strategic priorities, gaining exposure to complex business challenges, executive decision-making, and enterprise-wide initiatives while strengthening their ability to lead organizations, shape strategy, and influence outcomes at scale.

Program Experience

Participants will complete strategic rotational assignments aligned with enterprise priorities, gaining exposure to complex business challenges, business critical decision-making, and organizational leadership across Holman. Through executive engagement, targeted leadership development, mentoring, and cohort learning experiences, participants will strengthen their ability to shape strategy, lead through complexity and build enterprise-wide relationships.

Program Focus

Enterprise leadership
Strategic thinking and execution
Organizational effectiveness
Executive influence and stakeholder management
Talent strategy and succession planning
Leading large-scale change

Successful Candidates Demonstrate

Strong strategic and enterprise thinking capabilities
Proven success in leading leaders and developing organizational talent
Ability to influence executive stakeholders and drive alignment
Strong business and financial acumen
Experience leading through complexity, ambiguity, and change
Executive presence and communication skills
Ability to balance functional expertise with enterprise priorities
Systems thinking and organizational leadership capability
Proven ability to deliver transformational business outcomes
Commitment to continuous learning and leadership growth

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required
7+ years of leadership experience with responsibility for leading teams, functions, or significant business initiatives
Demonstrated success leading managers and/or large cross-functional teams
Track record of delivering measurable business results
Experience influencing senior leaders and driving organizational change
Ability to operate effectively in complex, matrixed environments
Willingness to travel to support rotational assignments
Demonstrated commitment to development of self and others

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading leaders, including manager or director-level talent
Strategic planning and business transformation experience
Enterprise or multi-functional leadership experience
MBA or advanced degree
Experience presenting to executive leadership teams or boards
Exposure to mergers, acquisitions, large-scale change initiatives, or enterprise strategy work

Program Commitment

Participants are expected to actively engage in all aspects of the Holman Leadership Rotation Program, including rotational assignments, leadership development experiences, mentoring, and cohort learning. Successful participants demonstrate a commitment to continuous growth, adaptability, and expanding their leadership capabilities through diverse experiences across Holman.

Pay:

We offer competitive wages that are commensurate with job-related skills, experience, relevant education or training, and geographic location, starting in the range of $178,340.00 - $276,425.00 CAD annually for full time employees. The annual compensation range is comprised of base pay and bonus earnings.

vide rewarding careers and better lives for employees and their families. We hire, train, empower, and reward exceptional people. To be better, we have to do better, and to do better we must know better. That’s why we are listening, open to learning new things – about ourselves and each other. We will never stop striving for improved diversity, equity, and inclusion because we are successful together when we feel trusted and supported. It’s The Holman Way.

About Lifemark Health Group – Stronger Than Ever

At Lifemark, we’re more than a healthcare company — we’re a movement. With clinics across Canada, we’re leading the way in injury recovery, patient care, and prevention. Our teams are united by one purpose: “Movement to a Better Life.”

When you join us, you’re not just taking on a job — you’re becoming part of a mission-driven, people-first culture where your leadership helps communities thrive.

Your Opportunity: Bring your difference. Make a difference
.

We’re looking for a dynamic, purpose-driven Regional Director to lead operations across Calgary and surrounding. In this role, you’ll inspire and empower Clinic Directors, create environments where people love to work, and ensure that patients receive the best care possible.

This is a role where strategy meets heart — and where agility, creativity, and solution-focused thinking are essential. You’ll drive growth, champion inclusivity, and set the stage for a healthier future in the communities we serve.

Lead and inspire Clinic Directors, building high-performing teams rooted in inclusivity and collaboration.
Elevate care by ensuring every clinic delivers consistent, top-tier patient experiences that reflect Lifemark’s mission.
Use data-driven insights to fuel revenue, EBITDA, and operational excellence.
Shape culture by fostering belonging, teamwork, and interdisciplinary care.
Build strong relationships with clinicians, leaders, and partners — positioning Lifemark as the top choice for talent and future acquisitions.
Manage budgets, KPIs, and resources with accountability and excellence.
Ensure compliance with all regulations, maintaining Lifemark’s strong reputation.

What you bring:

A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Physiotherapy, Allied Health, Business, or a related field.
7–10 years of senior management experience leading sizable, diverse teams.
Multi-unit experience preferably in a healthcare environment or connected industry
A proven track record in operations, strategy, and driving business growth.
Inclusive leadership skills that build trust, empower others, and inspire results.
Strong agility and the ability to adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment.
A creative, solution-oriented approach with the confidence to think outside the box when challenges arise.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.
Experience driving success in complex, evolving environments.

Why Join Lifemark?

When you join us, you get more than a role — you get to grow, lead, and thrive.

Nationally recognized brand with a strong digital presence and solid financials
Competitive compensation with a comprehensive Flex Benefits package (health, dental, and more)
$1500 annual continuing education allowance
30% Shoppers Drug Mart employee discount

Employee Stock Purchase Plan
A workplace culture built on mentorship, collaboration, and purpose
The opportunity to increase access to healthcare in Canada and leave a lasting impact

jobs.title: Chief Growth Officer & Head of Industries
jobs.description:
We are seeking a talented individual to join our Growth team, part of our Risk business at Marsh. This role will be based in Toronto. This is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.

As Chief Growth Officer & Head of Industries
you will drive market share expansion across Canada. This executive role is accountable for leading national new business growth, strengthening our presence in key markets, and elevating how we engage with the business community.

As a member of the Executive Committee, you will help shape national strategy, contribute to broader business priorities, and ensure growth remains embedded across the organization. You will lead a team of Producers and Industry Leaders while also maintaining a strong personal presence in the market.

A significant portion of growth will come from close partnership with Segment Leaders—shaping client strategies, identifying opportunities, and bringing a more proactive, growth-oriented lens to existing relationships. You will also be accountable for advancing our industry strategy, deepening intellectual capital, strengthening industry-led sales support, and enhancing our external market presence.

Our approach to growth is grounded in a simple belief: when we solve the right problems for clients, growth follows
. This role requires a shift from a traditional insurance-led approach to an enterprise-focused one—bringing the full breadth of our capabilities across risk and insurance, people, strategy, and capital to help clients address their most important business challenges.

We will count on you to:

Drive National Growth and Market Share

Develop and execute a national growth agenda focused on expanding market share across Canada.
Identify priority markets, industries, and target clients to drive sustained new business growth.
Assess competitive dynamics and define clear strategies to improve positioning and win rates.

Lead New Business Development

Build and advance a strong, diversified pipeline of new business opportunities.
Personally lead or sponsor high-impact pursuits where executive presence improves the likelihood of success.
Ensure a disciplined approach to opportunity qualification, pipeline management, and forecasting.
Anchor client conversations in understanding and solving the most relevant business challenges.

Activate the Client Team to Unlock Growth

Partner closely with Segment Leaders to shape client strategies and identify growth opportunities.
Bring a proactive, enterprise-wide lens to client relationships, expanding beyond traditional insurance discussions.
Align teams around priority pursuits and ensure a coordinated, client-centric approach to winning.

Expand to Full Firm Capability

Bring the full breadth of the firm’s capabilities to clients across risk and insurance, people, strategy, and capital.
Foster a culture of curiosity about clients’ broader enterprise challenges.
Identify opportunities beyond traditional insurance placements and connect clients to the right expertise.
Position the firm as a partner solving business problems, not just placing coverage.

Build a Strong External Presence

Act as a visible and credible leader across Canada.
Develop and maintain relationships with senior business leaders, centers of influence, and key stakeholders.
Lead by example in building trust, creating access, and converting relationships into growth opportunities.
Coach and enable Producers and Industry Leaders to strengthen their external presence and effectiveness.

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

Lead, coach, and develop a team of Producers and Industry Leaders focused on new client acquisition.
Set clear expectations for market activity, relationship building, and performance outcomes.
Build capability in consultative selling, executive engagement, and translating client needs into meaningful solutions.
Foster a culture of accountability, momentum, and continuous improvement.

Lead Strategic Pursuits and RFPs

Provide leadership on major pursuits and RFPs across the country.
Shape win strategies, value propositions, and executive-level messaging.
Ensure disciplined execution, clear accountability, and differentiation in competitive processes.

Contribute to Executive Committee Leadership

Serve as a key member of the Executive Committee, contributing to national strategy and business priorities.
Ensure growth considerations are embedded in broader decision-making across the country.
Partner with Segment Leaders to align priorities, remove barriers, and accelerate growth.

Drive Execution, Metrics, and Accountability

Establish and track clear growth metrics, including pipeline strength, win rates, and market share.
Use data and market insight to refine strategy and reallocate focus as needed.
Drive a culture of execution excellence, visibility, and results.

What you need to have:

Proven track record of driving new business growth and expanding market share

jobs.title: Director of Product, Logistics
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview

About the Team

Instacart’s Logistics Product team owns the multi-sided fulfillment engine that powers every order on the platform. We deliver fast and affordable delivery and pickup for customers; flexible, reliable, and competitive earnings for shoppers; and continuously improving efficiency and quality for the marketplace as a whole. Logistics runs on ML and optimization at its core — how we batch orders, match them to shoppers, position and pay shoppers for their work, and route them physically — making this one of the most technically deep and commercially consequential product areas at Instacart.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Director of Product to lead the Logistics product organization and take it to its next phase of growth. This is a highly visible leadership role with executive sponsorship, owning a pillar with company-wide impact on Instacart’s long-term growth and profitability. You will set the multi-year vision and strategy for Logistics, lead and grow a team of product managers, and partner closely with engineering, machine learning, data science, and operations to build products that generate value for all sides of the marketplace. You will be responsible for key outcomes core to the company’s success — fulfillment cost, speed, quality, and shopper experience — and trusted to make fast, high-quality decisions in a complex, ambiguous, and highly interconnected domain.

About The Job

Own the multi-year product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Logistics — spanning service coverage, delivery speed, order batching and routing, shopper matching, positioning, and pay — and drive cross-company momentum behind it.
Partner with the company’s executive leadership to define, prioritize, and deliver the strategy, translating complex, interconnected tradeoffs into crisp narratives that align the organization.
Solve complex fulfillment problems and build 0-to-1 products and services that create synergistic value across customers, shoppers, and retailers, while continuously improving efficiency, speed, and quality at scale.
Lead, hire, develop, and grow a high-performing team of product managers; establish operating rhythms, hiring plans, and development frameworks that build a healthy, high-trust team and develop leaders who set the pace.
Act as a trusted partner to engineering and ML leadership on complex, high-stakes technical tradeoffs; anticipate where to focus the team ahead of the business impact becoming obvious.
Define clear success metrics and maintain a rigorous experimentation portfolio with a consistent cadence, using data, first-principles thinking, and user research to make sound, sometimes irreversible, tradeoffs.
Lead cross-org initiatives that measurably improve org health, and mentor and uplevel PMs across the broader organization.

About You

Minimum Qualifications

10+ years of product management or similar experience, including 4+ years managing and developing product managers (including senior PMs).
Strong marketplace or systems thinking — the ability to reason about multi-sided marketplace interactions and long-term vs. short-term tradeoffs, heavily informed by data as well as user research.
Proven track record leading multi-quarter initiatives and delivering impactful products measured by hard business outcomes (e.g., cost, speed, quality).
Strong technical fluency with ML- and algorithms-driven products; comfortable working through complex technical tradeoffs alongside engineering and ML leaders.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to influence executive leadership and align cross-functional teams in a complex domain.
Demonstrated ability to hire, develop, and retain high-performing PMs and build healthy, high-trust teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a multi-sided dynamic marketplace-oriented role, envisioning or evaluating algorithms-based products and services.
Background in logistics, fulfillment, supply chain, or operationally complex physical environments.
Experience with e-commerce or grocery technology.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here. Currently, we are only hiring in the following provinces: Ontario, Alberta, British Columbia, and Nova Scotia.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

For Canadian based candidates, the base pay ranges for a successful candidate are listed below.

jobs.title: Food & Beverage Operations Director
jobs.description:
Grow with us...

Life at Starwood Hotels is based on a simple idea: the world is beautiful and we want to keep it that way. But we can’t do it alone. That’s why hiring thoughtful and inspiring Team Members and Leaders who understand that our people, collaboration, stellar service, and respect for nature are so important to us.

Food & Beverage is at the heart of the guest experience, and we are looking for an inspiring and commercially driven Food & Beverage Operations Director
to lead our operation. You will be responsible for the overall performance of our F&B outlets, combining exceptional service, strong financial performance, and innovative thinking to create memorable experiences for our guests.

As the Food & Beverage Operations Director
, you will lead, motivate, and develop the F&B leadership team while maintaining a highly visible presence across the operation. You will work closely with the Executive Chef, Executive Team, Sales & Marketing, and wider hotel leadership to continuously evolve our offering, maximise revenue, and ensure the highest standards of service, quality, and compliance

Job Responsibilities

Operational & Guest Experience

Take overall responsibility for the day-to-day operation and performance of all Food & Beverage outlets.
Maintain a highly visible, hands-on presence across the operation, ensuring service, presentation, atmosphere, and guest experience consistently meet our standards.
Set clear expectations for the F&B leadership team and hold leaders accountable for delivering exceptional service.
Monitor food, beverage, and service quality, responding quickly to guest feedback and operational challenges.
Ensure full compliance with Food Hygiene, Health & Safety, Licensing, and hotel policies and procedures.

People & Leadership

Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing Food & Beverage leadership team.
Create a culture of accountability, recognition, collaboration, and continuous feedback.
Coach and develop Outlet and Department Managers across leadership, financial management, cost control, forecasting, and revenue generation.
Lead by example, building strong relationships with colleagues and creating an environment where teams are empowered to contribute and succeed.

Commercial & Financial Performance

Take overall accountability for the financial performance and profitability of the Food & Beverage operation.
Review budgets, forecasts, payroll, P&Ls, and outlet performance, taking proactive action to achieve financial targets.
Identify opportunities to increase revenue and profitability through promotions, upselling, events, product development, and innovative experiences.
Maintain strong controls around stock, purchasing, labour, and operational costs.
Oversee capital expenditure and ensure projects are delivered effectively and in line with company guidelines.

Strategy & Innovation

Continuously challenge the current operation and identify opportunities to improve performance, efficiency, and guest satisfaction.
Work closely with the Executive Chef to develop innovative F&B strategies and remain relevant within the local and regional market.
Stay ahead of market trends and guest preferences, introducing new products, services, and experiences.
Partner with Sales & Marketing to drive promotions, events, and initiatives that increase awareness and revenue.
Build strong relationships within the local community and hospitality industry, representing the hotel at relevant events and functions.

About You...

Passionate about Food & Beverage with a m
inimum of 4 years’ experience leading a high-volume Food & Beverage operation, with responsibility for significant revenue performance.

Expert knowledge of Food & Beverage operations, with a proven track record of strong guest experience, team engagement, and financial performance.
An inspirational and commercially focused leader who can motivate, develop, and empower high-performing teams.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build strong relationships at all levels.
Highly flexible and able to meet the demands of a 24-hour hotel operation, including evenings, weekends, and holidays when required.

Why Choose Us?

Our Culture Is Caring, Thoughtful, And Rooted In Purpose. We Deliver Informed, Good-natured Service Perfectly Executed To Create Fulfillment And Well-being For Both Guests And Team Members. As Part Of Our Team, You Can Look Forward To

Career Advancement: Were growing rapidly and with growth comes advancement opportunities (around the globe)!
Team Member Recognition program - Earn rewards and pay it forward, while doing all the good you can

If you’re ready to lead with passion, elevate guest experiences, and shape the future of one of London’s most exciting dining destinations, we’d love to hear from you

About Us...

As a mission-driven company, our purpose is our true north, and our compass guides the way. The purpose we live by impacts the lives of our team members, drives the experiences for our guests, builds community with like-minded travelers and takes care of the planet we live in. new_jobs.title: Director, Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations
new_jobs.description:
Director, Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations – Canada

Expleo Group Canada | Montreal, Quebec | Onsite

Build the business. Lead the team. Open new markets.

Expleo Group Canada is seeking an accomplished, commercially driven Director of Engineering/Aerospace Business Development & Operations
to lead our Canadian aerospace operations and accelerate our expansion into professional engineering and technical services.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced engineering business development professional who combines the commercial instincts of a proven new-business hunter with the leadership capabilities of an effective operational manager.

We are seeking a player-coach - someone who can personally develop and close new business while leading a small team, strengthening customer relationships, elevating operational standards, and building a high-performance culture.

Our Canadian business has an established presence supporting aerospace production, assembly, manufacturing, and technical operations. Our next phase of growth is focused on expanding into higher-value engineering and professional technical services, including engineering staffing, specialized technical consulting, and project-based engineering solutions.

The successful candidate will bring established engineering or aerospace industry knowledge
, executive-level business presence, a strong understanding of engineering staffing and services, and a demonstrated history of opening new customer relationships.

This is not a position for someone who wants to manage an existing portfolio from behind a desk. We need a leader who can run the business while actively creating its next phase of growth.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering / Aerospace Business Development & Market Expansion (80% focus)

Lead executive-level customer discussions, strategic business reviews, commercial negotiations, and major account development initiatives.
Personally identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities with aerospace OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, and other aerospace and aviation organizations.
Leverage established industry relationships to gain access to engineering directors, program leaders, procurement executives, and senior decision-makers.
Develop new customer relationships through proactive prospecting, strategic networking, direct outreach, referrals, and in-person engagement.
Develop a qualified pipeline of new engineering business and consistently deliver measurable growth in revenue and profitability.
Build a sustainable market presence that positions Expleo as a credible engineering and technical services partner within the Canadian aerospace industry.

Canadian Operations & Business Leadership (20% focus)

Provide hands-on leadership for account team.
Lead, coach, and develop local account management teams, working with HR to establish clear expectations for performance, accountability, professionalism, and customer service.
Strengthen operational discipline, customer responsiveness, business communication, and leadership effectiveness across the Canadian organization.
Establish a consistent, professional, and commercially focused approach to customer meetings, business reviews, escalations, and operational reporting.
Oversee customer account performance, service delivery commitments, resource planning, and business profitability in partnership with delivery, recruiting, finance, and HR.
Build a collaborative, results-oriented culture that balances strong customer service with commercial growth and operational excellence.
Ensure effective coordination between local operations and Expleo's broader North American and global leadership teams.
Provide regular business performance updates and strategic recommendations to North American leadership.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in aerospace business development, engineering staffing, technical consulting, or engineering services, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
Proven success personally developing and closing new aerospace engineering staffing or professional technical services business.
Strong understanding of white-collar aerospace engineering disciplines, technical workforce requirements, and the commercial models used in engineering staffing and outsourced services.
Demonstrated experience leading a branch, regional operation, business unit, or commercial team with accountability for business growth and operational performance.
Established knowledge of the Canadian aerospace market, particularly the Quebec and Montreal aerospace ecosystem.
Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior engineering, operations, procurement, and executive stakeholders.
Proven ability to generate new opportunities independently rather than relying primarily on inbound requisitions or existing customer relationships.
Experience managing revenue targets, sales pipelines, commercial negotiations, account profitability, and business performance.
Strong leadership capabilities, including coaching, performance management, team development, and the ability to establish accountability.
Executive-level communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
Ability to balance strategic business development with hands-on operational leadership.
Professional fluency in French and English, both written and spoken, subject to the documented requirements of the position. French is essential for leading local operations and communicating with Quebec-based employees and customers. English is required for regular business discussions, commercial negotiations, and collaboration with customers and leadership outside Quebec, where these responsibilities cannot reasonably be reassigned.
Legally authorized to work in Canada without requiring employer immigration sponsorship.
Willing to work regularly on-site in the Montreal office and travel to customer locations as business needs require.
a multinational engineering, aerospace, or consulting organization.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Management, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

The Leader We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who brings both commercial credibility and operational leadership.
You have personally opened doors, developed relationships with engineering decision-makers, negotiated business, and delivered measurable sales results.
You are equally comfortable presenting to an aerospace executive, visiting a customer production facility, coaching an account manager, and addressing an operational performance issue.
You understand that leadership requires visibility, accountability, professionalism, and follow-through.
Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to build a business - not simply maintain one.
